question.text: Ramesh, aged 52, is in the pre-retirement stage. What percentage of his portfolio should ideally be in lower-risk products?

explanation.text: The Logic: In the pre-retirement stage (typically the final 5-10 years before retirement), capital preservation takes priority over aggressive growth. A common rule-of-thumb glide path tilts the portfolio progressively toward lower-risk, income-oriented products — broadly around 60-70% in lower-risk instruments — to reduce sequence-of-returns risk just before the income-drawdown phase begins. The Trap: Allocations like 25-30% or 40-50% in lower-risk products leave too much in volatile growth assets so close to retirement; conversely, 80-90% is closer to a deep-retirement defensive allocation and may unduly sacrifice long-term inflation protection in the pre-retirement window. Note: The specific 60-70% lower-risk allocation for the pre-retirement stage is not stated in the cited NISM Series XVII workbook pages, which qualitatively describe a shift toward lower-risk products as retirement approaches. The framing above reflects general retirement-planning glide-path heuristics rather than a direct workbook citation.
